document: ph1 analysis plan - written before any model is fit
label: POST-HOC (ph1): not pre-registered; reported separately from pre-registered results
plan: ph1 — POST-HOC analysis (not pre-registered). Question: does the metadata-only result of v0.2.1/v0.3 (H1, H2; fold 9; confirmatory-after-the-fact) hold on the test fold? Design: identical to v0.2.1 (decision table: blocks B0–B5, LogisticRegression and HistGradientBoosting, seeds as in v0.2.1) and v0.3 (H2 paired test: delta = macro-AUROC(B3) − macro-AUROC(B1); LogisticRegression primary, HistGradientBoosting seed 42 robustness), with exactly one change: training rows = folds 1–9 (instead of 1–8), evaluation rows = fold 10 (instead of 9). Encoder and scalers are fit on the training rows. Bootstrap: patient level, the locked fold-10 BOOT_IDX (N_BOOT 2000, BOOT_SEED 7) shared with the v0.9 analysis. Rules applied post hoc, unchanged: difference test (95% percentile CI of the paired delta excludes 0), TOST with SESOI_H2 = 0.02 (90% percentile CI within ±0.02), achieved equivalence bound; learner disagreement is reported, never resolved by selection. Nothing else is computed. All results are reported regardless of outcome, labelled post hoc, separately from the pre-registered results. Validation gate: before any fold-10 model is fit, the same code with training folds 1–8 and evaluation fold 9 must reproduce the v0.2.1 decision table and the v0.3 H2 results to within 1e-12; otherwise the run stops.
amendment_r2: r2 (2026-10-05): the r1 run stopped at the Part A gate because the LogisticRegression B2_acquisition rows (all three seeds; classes MI, CD, HYP) differed from v0.2.1 by at most 2.9e-6 (AUROC) and 5.7e-5 (AUPRC), attributed to the scipy 1.11.4 -> 1.15.3 change of the L-BFGS-B implementation; every other metric row and decision-table row (all HistGradientBoosting rows, LogisticRegression B0/B1/B3/B4/B5) and all H2 fields and per-draw deltas reproduced to 1e-12. The gate tolerance for the LogisticRegression B2_acquisition rows only was set to 1e-5 (AUROC, CIs) and 1e-4 (AUPRC) before anything was computed on fold 10. r1 attempt: outputs\ph1_failed_1.
self_sha256_procedure: Load the JSON file; remove the key 'self_sha256' (the key must be absent, not empty); serialize the remaining dict with json.dumps(d, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(',', ':')); compute SHA-256 of the UTF-8 bytes; the hex digest must equal the stored 'self_sha256'. (At write time numpy scalars were converted to plain JSON types first, so the loaded file hashes identically.)
